title: National Green Hydrogen Mission Advances Green Hydrogen Adoption in Petroleum and Refining Sector
body_text:
The Government of India is implementing the National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM) with the objective of making India a global hub for production, usage and export of green hydrogen and its derivatives.
Under the SIGHT (Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition) Mode - 2B scheme of the NGHM, Green Hydrogen production capacity of 30 Kilo Tonnes Per Annum (KTPA) has been awarded for refineries as per following details:
Refinery Location Green Hydrogen Production Capacity Indian Oil Corporation Limited Panipat 10 KTPA Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited Bina 5 KTPA Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited Vizag 5 KTPA Numaligarh Refineries Limited Numaligarh 10 KTPA Total 30 KTPA
The projects are implemented through BOO (Build Own Operate) arrangements through private developers, with project – specific investments by the concerned project developers. Domestic production and utilization of Green Hydrogen is expected to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels, enhance energy security and support India’s clean energy transition and net – zero objectives.
This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

ministry.name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy informed the Rajya Sabha that under the SIGHT Mode-2B scheme of the National Green Hydrogen Mission, 30 KTPA of green hydrogen production capacity has been awarded to four refineries: IOCL Panipat (10 KTPA), BPCL Bina (5 KTPA), HPCL Vizag (5 KTPA), and Numaligarh Refineries (10 KTPA). These projects will be implemented via Build-Own-Operate (BOO) arrangements by private developers with project-specific investments. The initiative aims to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels and support India's energy security and net-zero goals.
enrichment.context: The National Green Hydrogen Mission was approved by the Union Cabinet in January 2023 with an outlay of over Rs 19,700 crore, aiming to make India a global hub for green hydrogen production, usage, and export, and to help achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2070. The Mission targets at least 5 Million Metric Tonnes per annum of green hydrogen production capacity by 2030, with associated renewable energy capacity addition of about 125 GW. The SIGHT scheme is a key financial incentive mechanism under the Mission, structured into two components: Mode 2A for electrolyser manufacturing and Mode 2B for green hydrogen production, targeting hard-to-abate sectors like refining and fertilizers where hydrogen is currently sourced from fossil fuels (grey hydrogen). Refineries are significant hydrogen consumers used in desulphurization and other refining processes, so replacing grey hydrogen with green hydrogen (produced via electrolysis using renewable electricity) can substantially cut carbon emissions in the petroleum sector. This development is part of India's broader clean energy transition strategy, complementing other initiatives like PM-KUSUM, National Solar Mission, and India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement, while also addressing energy security concerns given India's heavy reliance on crude oil imports.

prelims_questions.question: The SIGHT (Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition) scheme mentioned in news is a component of which of the following?
prelims_questions.explanation: The SIGHT scheme is a financial incentive mechanism implemented under the National Green Hydrogen Mission to promote domestic manufacturing of electrolysers and production of green hydrogen.

prelims_questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Green Hydrogen Mission's SIGHT Mode-2B scheme:
1. It provides incentives for electrolyser manufacturing only.
2. Projects under this mode are being implemented through Build-Own-Operate arrangements by private developers.
3. Refineries are among the sectors targeted for green hydrogen adoption under this scheme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: SIGHT Mode-2B is for green hydrogen production (not electrolyser manufacturing, which is Mode-2A), and the projects awarded to refineries like IOCL, BPCL, HPCL, and NRL are being implemented through BOO arrangements by private developers, making statements 2 and 3 correct while statement 1 is incorrect.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the National Green Hydrogen Mission in achieving India's energy security and net-zero emission targets. Highlight the role of the petroleum refining sector in this transition.
Examine the challenges and opportunities in scaling up green hydrogen production in India's hard-to-abate industrial sectors such as refining and fertilizers.
